stem: Why can nutrient mobility within the plant help with diagnosis?
choices: It can influence whether deficiency symptoms appear first on older or newer tissue, providing one clue that should be combined with other evidence
Mobile nutrients tend to create recognizable symptoms in flowers before other tissues, so flower symptoms can be used to identify which mobile element is deficient without root-zone measurements
Immobile nutrients remain concentrated near the root zone rather than moving into developing tissues, so low values in young-leaf samples mainly reflect limited transport from the medium
Nutrient mobility determines how strongly roots acidify or alkalize the medium, so the position of symptoms can be used as a direct indicator of root-zone pH
rationale: Plants can redistribute some nutrients more readily than others. Symptom location can therefore provide diagnostic information, but it should be interpreted with stage, root-zone conditions, and other evidence.
